title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has responded to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards by outlining steps to improve transparency, accountability, and safety in AI systems. It emphasises the development of new standards, regulatory frameworks, and oversight mechanisms to ensure that AI technologies serve the public interest.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The EU Regulation 2024/1689 sets out harmonised rules for AI across the EU, covering safety, transparency, and compliance requirements for AI systems. It also updates and amends existing regulations and directives to ensure they align with these new AI standards, aiming to protect consumers while encouraging responsible innovation.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines how it will oversee the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to keep assessments fair, transparent, and secure for all learners. The policy was issued at the request of the Secretary of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade to guide exam bodies and industry partners in responsibly deploying AI tools.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how AI systems use copyrighted works, weighing the legal and ethical risks for creators and developers. It offers recommendations to protect copyright holders while enabling responsible AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report on artificial intelligence, outlining its commitments and future plans. It stresses the need to avoid complacency and highlights specific actions the government will take to support responsible AI development and deployment across the UK.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the purpose, scope and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing the intersection of artificial intelligence and public standards. It includes frequently asked questions to clarify the committee’s role and expectations for its work.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of Artificial Intelligence. In its submission, the organization outlines key concerns and proposes recommendations for improving AI oversight and regulation.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how the use of AI alters the rules and oversight needed for medical products, aiming to keep them safe and effective. It provides guidance on applying the AI White Paper principles to create clear, transparent regulations for developers and regulators.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our country the most effective, efficient, trusted and influential defence organisation in AI for a nation of our size. It focuses on leveraging AI to strengthen operational capabilities, enhance safety, and uphold strong ethical and safety standards.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan details how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to take advantage of AI’s benefits. It also outlines steps to manage and mitigate potential risks, ensuring AI is used safely and responsibly across transportation services.
